factors.label: No income recorded
factors.detail: Runway assumes zero income. Add your income streams (salary, part-time work, allowance, scholarship) if you have any.

factors.label: Monthly spending baseline
factors.detail: ₩500,000 essential + ₩0 discretionary per month, averaged over the last 40 days of logged expenses (including transit).

factors.label: Liquid savings not set
factors.detail: A runway needs a starting balance. Add your liquid savings (cash and accounts you can withdraw from immediately) to compute it.

assumptions: Month-by-month simulation; within a month, money is assumed to flow evenly, so a partial month is the fraction of that month's shortfall the remaining savings could cover.
Essential categories: groceries, transportation, housing & utilities, education. Everything else is discretionary and is the only spending the 'with cuts' scenario reduces.

Spending baseline is the daily average of the last 90 days of logged expenses (including transit), scaled to 30.44 days per month, once at least 28 days are logged; before that, the monthly budget is used.
Savings earn no interest and no new borrowing is assumed: runway ends when savings reach zero.
A currency devaluation reduces only income streams paid in that currency; savings are held in KRW.
For attribution, a scenario whose savings never run out is scored at the horizon length, so shocks that don't exhaust savings within the horizon can be under-credited.
Risk level uses the 3-6 month emergency-fund rule of thumb on the shocked runway: under 3 months is high, under 6 is moderate.
